      - "Emphasise whole foods: vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, nuts, seeds, fatty fish."
      - "Include omega-3 sources 2-3x/week (e.g. salmon, mackerel) or flax/chia daily."
      - "Prioritise colourful anti-inflammatory vegetables daily (leafy greens, berries, cruciferous veg)."
      - "Use extra virgin olive oil as primary fat; include avocados and nuts."
      - "Limit processed foods, refined sugars, and trans fats."
      - "Prefer low-FODMAP options on flare and flow days if sensitive; reduce fibre if discomfort occurs."
      - "Stay hydrated: aim for ~2L/day adjusted for activity and symptoms."
      - "Distribute protein across meals: target ~20-30g protein per main meal."
      - "Include fermented foods for gut support (yoghurt, kefir, sauerkraut) as tolerated."
      - "Moderate caffeine and alcohol; avoid alcohol during flare and flow days."
    SAMPLE_MEALS:
      - "Breakfast: Oats with berries, chia, walnuts, and yogurt or plant milk; cinnamon."
      - "Lunch: Mixed leafy salad with quinoa, roasted vegetables, chickpeas, olive oil and lemon; grilled salmon twice weekly."
      - "Snack: Apple with almond butter or carrot sticks with hummus."
      - "Dinner: Grilled fatty fish or lentil stew, steamed green vegetables, roasted sweet potato."
      - "Pre-workout snack: Banana or rice cake with peanut butter (30-60m before session)."
      - "Post-workout: Protein-rich meal or shake within 1-2h (20-30g protein) with carbs and vegetables."
    ADJUSTMENTS:
      - "On flare and flow days (2026-07-10 to 2026-07-13 and 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-07 and on menstrual flow days): reduce intensity (use lower RPE), avoid HIIT, jumping, and heavy Valsalva; choose lower-impact aerobic sessions (walking, cycling, swimming) and prioritize rest and heat/anti-spasm nutrition (warm broths, ginger, turmeric)."
      - "If gastrointestinal symptoms occur, opt for simple, low-residue meals (white rice, cooked carrots, plain protein) until symptoms ease."
      - "Consider consulting a dietitian for supplementation (omega-3, vitamin D) tailored to bloodwork."

  PHASE "Anti-inflammatory nutrition" (12 weeks):
    GUIDELINES:
      - "Emphasise whole foods: vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, nuts, seeds, fatty fish."
      - "Include omega-3 sources 2-3x/week (e.g. salmon, mackerel) or flax/chia daily."
      - "Prioritise colourful anti-inflammatory vegetables daily (leafy greens, berries, cruciferous veg)."
      - "Use extra virgin olive oil as primary fat; include avocados and nuts."
      - "Limit processed foods, refined sugars, and trans fats."
      - "Prefer low-FODMAP options on flare and flow days if sensitive; reduce fibre if discomfort occurs."
      - "Stay hydrated: aim for ~2L/day adjusted for activity and symptoms."
      - "Distribute protein across meals: target ~20-30g protein per main meal."
      - "Include fermented foods for gut support (yoghurt, kefir, sauerkraut) as tolerated."
      - "Moderate caffeine and alcohol; avoid alcohol during flare and flow days."
    SAMPLE_MEALS:
      - "Breakfast: Oats with berries, chia, walnuts, and yogurt or plant milk; cinnamon."
      - "Lunch: Mixed leafy salad with quinoa, roasted vegetables, chickpeas, olive oil and lemon; grilled salmon twice weekly."
      - "Snack: Apple with almond butter or carrot sticks with hummus."
      - "Dinner: Grilled fatty fish or lentil stew, steamed green vegetables, roasted sweet potato."
      - "Pre-workout snack: Banana or rice cake with peanut butter (30-60m before session)."
      - "Post-workout: Protein-rich meal or shake within 1-2h (20-30g protein) with carbs and vegetables."
    ADJUSTMENTS:
      - "On flare and flow days (2026-07-10 to 2026-07-13 and 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-07 and on menstrual flow days): reduce intensity (use lower RPE), avoid HIIT, jumping, and heavy Valsalva; choose lower-impact aerobic sessions (walking, cycling, swimming) and prioritize rest and heat/anti-spasm nutrition (warm broths, ginger, turmeric)."
      - "If gastrointestinal symptoms occur, opt for simple, low-residue meals (white rice, cooked carrots, plain protein) until symptoms ease."
      - "Consider consulting a dietitian for supplementation (omega-3, vitamin D) tailored to bloodwork."
